title: Job Chapter 18 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Job chapter 18 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Job Chapter 18 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Job Chapter 18.

questions.question: In Job 18, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The light of the wicked shall be put out
The steps of his strength shall be straitened
He teareth himself in his anger
questions.explanation: Bildad the Shuhite answers at the very start of the chapter in verse 1.

questions.question: Who answered in Job 18?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 states explicitly that Bildad the Shuhite answered.

questions.question: What does Bildad ask about in Job 18:2?
options: How long will ye make an end of words?
questions.correctAnswer: How long will ye make an end of words?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 contains the question 'How long will it be ere ye make an end of words?'

questions.question: According to Job 18:3, how are Bildad and his companions counted in Job's sight?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 states 'Wherefore are we counted as beasts, and reputed vile in your sight?'

questions.question: What does Bildad say about the earth and the rock in Job 18:4?
options: Shall the earth be forsaken for thee? shall the rock be removed out of his place?
The earth will shake and the rock will move
The earth is firm and the rock is unshaken
The earth will open and swallow the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: Shall the earth be forsaken for thee? shall the rock be removed out of his place?
questions.explanation: Verse 4 asks specifically if the earth will be forsaken and the rock moved for him.

questions.question: What happens to the light of the wicked according to Job 18:5?
options: The light of the wicked shall be put out
The light of the wicked shall shine brighter
The light of the wicked shall blind others
The light of the wicked shall remain
questions.correctAnswer: The light of the wicked shall be put out
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says 'Yea, the light of the wicked shall be put out.'

questions.question: In Job 18:6, what will happen to the candle of the wicked?
options: His candle shall be put out with him
His candle shall light the way
His candle shall be given to others
questions.correctAnswer: His candle shall be put out with him
questions.explanation: Verse 6 states, 'and his candle shall be put out with him.'

questions.question: What does Job 18:7 say about the steps of the wicked's strength?
options: The steps of his strength shall be straitened
The steps of his strength shall be mighty
The steps of his strength shall be swift
The steps of his strength shall be firm
questions.correctAnswer: The steps of his strength shall be straitened
questions.explanation: Verse 7 says, 'The steps of his strength shall be straitened.'

questions.question: Who is described as tearing himself in anger in Job 18:4?
questions.explanation: Verse 4 states 'He teareth himself in his anger,' referring to the subject in context.

questions.question: According to Job 18:2, what does Bildad suggest should happen before they speak?
options: Mark, and afterwards we will speak
questions.correctAnswer: Mark, and afterwards we will speak
questions.explanation: Verse 2 says, 'mark, and afterwards we will speak.'

questions.question: What will the spark of the wicked's fire do according to Job 18:5?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 states, 'and the spark of his fire shall not shine.'

questions.question: True or False: Bildad the Shuhite speaks in Job 18.
questions.explanation: Verse 1 clearly states, 'Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,' confirming he speaks.

questions.question: True or False: The candle of the wicked will be put out with him according to Job 18.
questions.explanation: Verse 6 states, 'and his candle shall be put out with him.'

questions.question: True or False: Job 18 says the wicked will be rewarded with riches.
questions.explanation: The chapter does not mention rewards or riches; rather, it speaks of the downfall of the wicked (Job 18:5-7).

questions.question: True or False: Job 18 describes the earth being moved from its place for the wicked.
questions.explanation: Verse 4 asks rhetorically if the earth or the rock will be moved for him, implying it will not be.

medium.title: Job Chapter 18 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Job Chapter 18 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What happens to the wicked according to Job 18:5?
options: Their light shall be put out
questions.correctAnswer: Their light shall be put out
questions.explanation: This is correct because Job 18:5 states that 'the light of the wicked shall be put out.'

questions.question: What does Job 18:9 promise will happen if someone is ensnared?
options: The snare will not catch him
The robber shall prevail against him
questions.correctAnswer: The robber shall prevail against him
questions.explanation: This is correct because Job 18:9 states that 'the robber shall prevail against him' when ensnared.

questions.question: According to Job 18:12, what shall be ready beside the wicked?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Job 18:12 states that 'destruction shall be ready at his side.'

questions.question: What does Job 18:10 say is laid for the wicked?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Job 18:10 states that 'the snare is laid for him in the ground.'

questions.question: What effect do terrors have on the wicked according to Job 18:11?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Job 18:11 states that 'terrors shall make him afraid on every side.'

questions.question: What does Job 18:14 say will happen to the confidence of the wicked?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Job 18:14 states that 'his confidence shall be rooted out of his tabernacle.'

questions.question: According to Job 18:7, what causes the steps of the wicked's strength to be straitened?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Job 18:7 states that 'his own counsel shall cast him down.'

questions.question: What does Job 18:13 say will devour the strength of the wicked?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Job 18:13 states that 'even the firstborn of death shall devour his strength.'

questions.question: What is indicated about the wicked's strength in Job 18:12?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Job 18:12 states that 'his strength shall be hungerbitten.'

questions.question: What do the words of Bildad in Job 18:2 suggest about his view on Job's suffering?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Bildad questions Job's words, indicating he thinks Job is unjustified in his suffering.

questions.question: What does Job 18:6 say will happen to the light in the wicked's tabernacle?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Job 18:6 states that 'the light shall be dark in his tabernacle, and his candle shall be put out with him.'

questions.question: The statement in Job 18:4 about tearing oneself in anger implies what about dealing with emotions?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Job 18:4 suggests that tearing oneself in anger can be destructive.

questions.question: Is it true that according to Job 18:5, the spark of the wicked's fire will shine forever?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Job 18:5 states that 'the spark of his fire shall not shine.'

questions.question: Is it true that Job 18:12 indicates that the wicked will experience abundance?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Job 18:12 states that 'his strength shall be hungerbitten,' indicating lack rather than abundance.

questions.question: Is it true that Job 18:9 implies that the wicked will have an easy path?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Job 18:9 indicates that the wicked will be caught in a snare, suggesting difficulty.

hard.title: Job Chapter 18 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Job Chapter 18.

questions.question: According to Job 18:15, why shall brimstone be scattered upon the habitation of the wicked?
options: Because it is none of his
questions.correctAnswer: Because it is none of his
questions.explanation: Job 18:15 states that brimstone shall be scattered upon his habitation because it is none of his, indicating a divine rejection of the wicked's dwelling.

questions.question: What happens to the roots and branches of the wicked according to Job 18:16?
options: His roots shall be dried up and his branch cut off
His roots shall grow deep and his branch flourish
His roots shall be watered and his branch be strong
His roots shall remain but his branch shall wither
questions.correctAnswer: His roots shall be dried up and his branch cut off
questions.explanation: Job 18:16 describes the fate of the wicked as having roots dried up beneath and branches cut off above, symbolizing complete destruction.

questions.question: What is said about the remembrance and name of the wicked in Job 18:17?
options: His remembrance shall perish and he shall have no name in the street
His remembrance shall be eternal and his name praised
His name shall be written in the book of life
His name shall be honored among his people
questions.correctAnswer: His remembrance shall perish and he shall have no name in the street
questions.explanation: Job 18:17 clearly states that the wicked's remembrance shall perish from the earth and he shall have no name in the street, indicating total obliteration of legacy.

questions.question: According to Job 18:18, where shall the wicked be driven?
options: From light into darkness, and chased out of the world
questions.correctAnswer: From light into darkness, and chased out of the world
questions.explanation: Job 18:18 says the wicked shall be driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world, implying exile and condemnation.

questions.question: Who shall the wicked have neither among his people, according to Job 18:19?
questions.explanation: Job 18:19 specifies that the wicked shall neither have son nor nephew among his people, highlighting the end of his family line.

questions.question: What reaction do those who come after the wicked have on his day, as described in Job 18:20?
options: They shall be astonied, as those before were affrighted
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be astonied, as those before were affrighted
questions.explanation: Job 18:20 describes that those who come after the wicked shall be astonied at his day, like those who went before were affrighted, showing fear and awe.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word 'tabernacle' (אֹהֶל, ohel) as used in Job 18:15?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'tabernacle' (אֹהֶל, ohel) in Job 18:15 refers to a tent or dwelling place, signifying a temporary home or shelter.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Job 18:5-14 to describe the fate of the wicked?
questions.explanation: Job 18:5-14 uses metaphor extensively, such as 'The light of the wicked shall be put out' to symbolize the destruction of the wicked's life and power.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to Job 18:5 about the extinguishing of the wicked's light?
questions.explanation: Psalm 37:20 echoes the theme of the wicked's destruction and end of their light, connecting closely with Job 18:5.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse reflects the theme of being driven from light into darkness as found in Job 18:18?
questions.explanation: John 3:19 discusses men loving darkness rather than light because their deeds are evil, echoing Job 18:18's imagery of being driven from light into darkness.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Job 18:15 in the chapter?
options: His confidence shall be rooted out of his tabernacle
The steps of his strength shall be straitened
Terrors shall make him afraid on every side
questions.correctAnswer: His confidence shall be rooted out of his tabernacle
questions.explanation: Job 18:14 states that his confidence shall be rooted out of his tabernacle, which immediately precedes 18:15.

questions.question: According to Job 18:21, what are the dwellings of the wicked described as?
options: The place of him that knoweth not God
A place of blessing and peace
A place of refuge and safety
A place of joy and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: The place of him that knoweth not God
questions.explanation: Job 18:21 clearly states that such are the dwellings of the wicked, and this is the place of him that knoweth not God, indicating separation from divine knowledge.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew term 'king of terrors' in Job 18:14 symbolize?
questions.explanation: The 'king of terrors' in Job 18:14 is a Hebrew euphemism for death, emphasizing its fearful and inescapable nature.

questions.question: How does Job 18:12-13 use personification to describe destruction?
options: Destruction is described as ready at his side and devouring strength
questions.correctAnswer: Destruction is described as ready at his side and devouring strength
questions.explanation: Job 18:12-13 personifies destruction as being ready at the side and devouring the strength of the wicked, making it an active and menacing force.

questions.question: True or False: Job 18:17 says that the wicked shall have a lasting name in the street.
questions.explanation: Job 18:17 states the opposite: the wicked shall have no name in the street, indicating their legacy will vanish.

theological.title: Job Chapter 18 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Job Chapter 18 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Job 18:5 teach about the fate of the wicked?
options: The light of the wicked shall be put out
The wicked shall be exalted by God
The wicked shall inherit the earth
The wicked shall receive immediate salvation
questions.correctAnswer: The light of the wicked shall be put out
questions.explanation: Job 18:5 states, 'Yea, the light of the wicked shall be put out,' indicating the doctrine that the wicked will face judgment and loss of life and blessing.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning human sin is emphasized in Job 18:8?
options: The wicked are ensnared by their own steps
Human sin can be overcome by human effort alone
Sin has no consequences in the present life
The wicked are exempt from divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked are ensnared by their own steps
questions.explanation: Job 18:8 says, 'For he is cast into a net by his own feet, and he walketh upon a snare,' teaching that human sin entraps the sinner by their own actions.

questions.question: What doctrine about the finality of divine justice is taught in Job 18:14?
options: The confidence of the wicked is rooted out and they face the king of terrors
The wicked will eventually repent and be restored
The king of terrors is a human judge
questions.correctAnswer: The confidence of the wicked is rooted out and they face the king of terrors
questions.explanation: Job 18:14 states, 'His confidence shall be rooted out of his tabernacle, and it shall bring him to the king of terrors,' teaching that divine judgment is final and terrifying for the wicked.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Job 18:4 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Job 18:4 says, 'shall the earth be forsaken for thee? and shall the rock be removed out of his place?' demonstrating God's sovereign control over creation.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is highlighted in Job 18:21?
questions.explanation: Job 18:21 states, 'Surely such are the dwellings of the wicked, and this is the place of him that knoweth not God,' emphasizing God's holiness and separation from sin.

questions.question: How does Job 18:17 connect to the broader biblical theme of legacy and remembrance?
options: It teaches that the wicked will have no lasting remembrance on earth
It promises eternal fame for all
It suggests that all will be remembered equally
It denies the existence of any afterlife
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that the wicked will have no lasting remembrance on earth
questions.explanation: Job 18:17 says, 'His remembrance shall perish from the earth, and he shall have no name in the street,' linking to biblical themes where legacy is tied to righteousness.

questions.question: In what way does Job 18:15 anticipate New Testament teachings about divine judgment?
options: It portrays judgment as an irreversible dwelling apart from God
It denies the reality of hell
It shows judgment as temporary and corrective
questions.correctAnswer: It portrays judgment as an irreversible dwelling apart from God
questions.explanation: Job 18:15 states, 'It shall dwell in his tabernacle, because it is none of his: brimstone shall be scattered upon his habitation,' which prefigures the concept of eternal separation from God in judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Job 18:6 and Job 18:10 teach about the consequences of wickedness?
options: The wicked experience darkness and traps laid for them
The wicked are shielded from harm
The wicked prosper despite their actions
The wicked are enlightened by their sin
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked experience darkness and traps laid for them
questions.explanation: Job 18:6 says, 'The light shall be dark in his tabernacle,' and Job 18:10 says, 'The snare is laid for him in the ground,' both describing judgment as darkness and entrapment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Job 18:12 and Job 18:13 teach regarding the nature of destruction for the wicked?
options: Destruction consumes the strength of the wicked like a consuming force
The wicked are immune to destruction
questions.correctAnswer: Destruction consumes the strength of the wicked like a consuming force
questions.explanation: Job 18:12 states, 'His strength shall be hungerbitten,' and 18:13, 'It shall devour the strength of his skin,' portraying destruction as consuming strength.

questions.question: What combined theological insight do Job 18:16 and Job 18:19 provide concerning the social and spiritual consequences of wickedness?
options: The wicked lose both their familial legacy and spiritual vitality
The wicked gain greater social influence
The wicked's family prospers despite their sin
The wicked are spiritually strengthened by their trials
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked lose both their familial legacy and spiritual vitality
questions.explanation: Job 18:16 says, 'His roots shall be dried up,' and 18:19 says, 'He shall neither have son nor nephew,' indicating loss of both life and legacy.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Job 18:11-13 suggests God arbitrarily terrifies people without cause. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Terrors come upon the wicked as just consequences of their sin
God terrifies all people equally regardless of their actions
Terrors are random and do not relate to sin
These verses teach that God is indifferent to human behavior
questions.correctAnswer: Terrors come upon the wicked as just consequences of their sin
questions.explanation: Job 18:11-13 describes terrors and destruction surrounding the wicked as consequences of their own sin, not arbitrary acts of God.

questions.question: What doctrine does Job 18:7 teach about human counsel in relation to sin and downfall?
options: One's own counsel can cause one's downfall
Human counsel is infallible and leads to salvation
Sin has no impact on human decisions
Human counsel is irrelevant to spiritual outcomes
questions.correctAnswer: One's own counsel can cause one's downfall
questions.explanation: Job 18:7 states, 'his own counsel shall cast him down,' teaching that wicked choices lead to self-destruction.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is illustrated in Job 18:12 concerning how God deals with human strength?
questions.explanation: Job 18:12 speaks of strength being 'hungerbitten' and destruction ready at his side, reflecting God's just punishment.

questions.question: How does Job 18:9 contribute to the biblical narrative about the inevitability of divine judgment?
options: The wicked are caught by snares and robbers, symbolizing inevitable judgment
The wicked can evade judgment through cleverness
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked are caught by snares and robbers, symbolizing inevitable judgment
questions.explanation: Job 18:9 says, 'The gin shall take him by the heel,' portraying the certainty of judgment over the wicked.

questions.question: What theological lesson does Job 18:20 teach about the fear of judgment across generations?
options: Both past and future generations are afraid of the day of judgment
Only the current generation fears judgment
Judgment is irrelevant to future generations
Fear of judgment will be replaced by hope in the future
questions.correctAnswer: Both past and future generations are afraid of the day of judgment
questions.explanation: Job 18:20 states that those who come after will be astonished and those before were affrighted, indicating universal fear of judgment.
